extraction.name: CommonCatalog
extraction.description: CommonCatalog is a dataset of roughly 70 million Creative-Commons-licensed (CC) images sourced from YFCC100M, paired with high-quality synthetic captions generated using a pre-trained BLIP-2 OPT2.5B model. The dataset is split into two subsets: CommonCatalog-C (approximately 26 million images licensed for commercial use) and CommonCatalog-NC (approximately 67 million images including non-commercial licenses). It was created to train text-to-image generative models without relying on web-scraped data of unclear provenance, addressing copyright concerns associated with datasets like LAION-2B.
extraction.license: Creative Commons (various CC licenses including CC-BY 2.0, CC-BY-SA 2.0, CC-BY-NC 2.0, CC-BY-NC-SA 2.0; excludes ND licenses)
extraction.creator: Aaron Gokaslan, A. Feder Cooper, Jasmine Collins, Landan Seguin, Austin Jacobson, Mihir Patel, Jonathan Frankle, Cory Stephenson, Volodymyr Kuleshov (Cornell Tech and Databricks Mosaic)
extraction.citeAs: Gokaslan, A., Cooper, A. F., Collins, J., Seguin, L., Jacobson, A., Patel, M., Frankle, J., Stephenson, C., & Kuleshov, V. (2023). CommonCanvas: An Open Diffusion Model Trained with Creative-Commons Images. arXiv:2310.16825v1 [cs.CV].
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were sourced from the YFCC100M dataset, which consists of 100 million CC-licensed images and multimedia files with Flickr IDs. The authors re-scraped these images from Flickr at very high resolution (exceeding 4K) based on IDs provided in the YFCC100M metadata. Images with non-derivative (ND) licenses were excluded. The remaining images were divided into commercial (C) and non-commercial (NC) subsets. Synthetic captions were then generated for all collected images using a pre-trained BLIP-2 OPT2.5B model, requiring approximately 1,120 GPU A100 hours.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Almost all CC images lack the captions necessary to train a high-quality text-to-image model. Of the images collected, only approximately 30-34% had any associated alt-text captions, and those that did often only included the image title or a URL rather than descriptive captions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data originates from the YFCC100M dataset, which consists of 100 million CC-licensed images and multimedia files sourced from Flickr. Images were re-scraped from Flickr at native high resolution (exceeding 4K) using Flickr IDs provided in the YFCC100M metadata.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The YFCC100M dataset is approximately a decade old as noted by the authors. The re-scraping and caption generation were conducted as part of this research, published October 25, 2023.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Missing captions were addressed through a transfer learning technique called 'telephoning': a pre-trained BLIP-2 OPT2.5B model was used to generate synthetic captions for all CC images that lacked captions. Images were center-cropped and resized to a maximum of 512x512 pixels before captioning.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images with non-derivative (ND) licenses were excluded from training. The remaining images were split into commercial (CommonCatalog-C) and non-commercial (CommonCatalog-NC) subsets based on their CC license type. For captioning, images were center-cropped and resized to a maximum of 512x512 pixels. At training time, all images remain in their native resolution.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were re-scraped from Flickr at native high resolution. Images with non-derivative licenses were excluded. For caption generation, images were center-cropped and resized to a maximum of 512x512 pixels. Synthetic captions were generated using BLIP-2 OPT2.5B. The dataset was split into commercial (C) and non-commercial (NC) subsets. At training time, images remain in native resolution. Latents were precomputed for the entire training dataset to amortize computation costs.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Captions were synthetically generated using the pre-trained BLIP-2 OPT2.5B model applied to each CC image. Images were center-cropped and resized to 512x512 pixels before captioning. BLIP-2 consists of a frozen visual encoder, a learned transformer network converting visual embeddings to text prompts, and a frozen large language model. The captioning process required approximately 1,120 GPU A100 hours.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: BLIP-2 OPT2.5B (pre-trained model used for automated caption generation)
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: BLIP-2 captions were found to be qualitatively more descriptive than corresponding LAION-2B ground-truth alt-text captions, which often contain product names, irrelevant details, or poor grammar. This was corroborated by Nguyen et al., which shows quantitatively (in terms of CLIP Score) that BLIP-2 captions are higher quality than ground-truth captions, at the cost of caption diversity. Reduced diversity of n-grams in synthetic captions was observed, reflected in a decrease in unique trigrams.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: BLIP-2 OPT2.5B (pre-trained image-to-text model used to generate synthetic captions for all CC images)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The CommonCatalog dataset of CC images and synthetic captions, along with trained CommonCanvas models and code, are released on HuggingFace and GitHub. The authors note that the YFCC100M data is about a decade old and plan to augment CommonCatalog with Creative-Commons images from other sources in future work. No explicit deprecation policy is stated.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains images of public figures and celebrities (e.g., Bill Gates, Elon Musk, Kim Kardashian, Barack Obama, Hillary Clinton). The dataset may also contain images of people's faces, as the model was evaluated on face generation categories.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and resulting models are intended to provide an alternative to web-scraped datasets with unclear copyright provenance, addressing legal and ethical concerns around training generative AI models. The work demonstrates that high-quality text-to-image models can be trained on openly licensed data, potentially reducing copyright infringement risks. The authors note that models trained on CC images are less likely to generate iconic copyrighted characters compared to models trained on web-scraped data. However, the authors acknowledge that even with CC-licensed training data, adversarial prompts can still produce content resembling iconic characters.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The YFCC100M source data is approximately a decade old, making it less current than LAION-2B. Synthetic captions generated by BLIP-2 exhibit reduced diversity of n-grams compared to ground-truth captions. The model underperforms in categories including faces, general photography, and paintings, which are categories originating from the Conceptual Captions dataset that relies on web-scraped data. CLIP-FID metrics may favor SD2 since CLIP is trained on a similar style of text as LAION, introducing potential evaluation bias.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset contains only approximately 70 million images, which is less than 3% the size of LAION-2B. The YFCC100M source data is about a decade old and may not reflect current image distributions. Synthetic captions exhibit reduced diversity compared to human-generated captions. Models trained on this dataset underperform in categories such as faces, general photography, and paintings. The dataset does not include images with non-derivative (ND) licenses. The authors note that the dataset may not be sufficient for fine-tuning models for specific categories without supplementation.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training text-to-image generative diffusion models; the dataset is intended as a copyright-safer alternative to web-scraped datasets like LAION-2B for training generative models. Two subsets are provided: CommonCatalog-C for commercial use cases and CommonCatalog-NC for non-commercial use cases. An evaluation set of BLIP-2 captions for non-derivative (ND) CC images is also released. The authors suggest the dataset could be supplemented with domain-specific datasets (e.g., FFHQ for faces) for fine-tuning.
